newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex takes step to become more businesslike.
newsitem.headline: Pemex takes step to become more businesslike.

text.p: Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) is planning to introduce performance-related contracts for its top officials to boost accountability and make the state oil giant more competitive with the private sector.
A top Pemex official told Reuters on Wednesday the proposal was aimed at bolstering performance targets that he said are currently outlined in a "looser way."

Pemex Chairman Adrian Lajous said Tuesday on the anniversary of the expropriation of the oil industry that the new contracts would boost efficiency in an increasingly competitive international market.
Lajous said the project was "feasible" as early as next year, "to coincide with a new phase of expansion for the petroleum industry."

Also to bolster effinciency, Lajous said the company continues to discuss with the energy and finance ministries ways to distance its daily operations and budgetary control from the federal government.
He and Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles have said Pemex needs more flexibility to make decisions, to be competitive with other private oil companies.
"A more business-like orientation in Pemex's daily actions is an essential requirement in its own development and for the competitiveness of the national industry," Lajous said.

Although the Pemex source noted advances have been slow, he said the process is difficult. The company is a key source of revenue for Mexico, providing more than a quarter of public income in 1996, and the Finance Ministry is reluctant to loosen its grip.
Lajous said the elimination of subsidies, scheduled to end when prices are freed on liquified petroleum gas (LPG) by July, is an important step in the company's independence from the state.
"The advantages of its monopoly position are limited because of the price regulation mechanism in place," he noted.

Another pressure the company faces is the force of the 130,000-member oil workers union, which on Tuesday called for less third-party contracting to protect jobs. Pemex has been moving in recent years to contract out more auxiliary projects to focus on its core business.
